verdict.rationale: Figma Make documents generating a server-side Payload/Next.js backend from chat, with a database, file storage, authentication and an admin panel. It can also connect a Supabase project and store keys securely so a published app can use them without exposing them to visitors. That covers the server-side and secret-handling core, but payments and email integrations are never shown. MCP connectivity only pulls in context for building, so it does not count as an app integration. Missing for 10: explicit server-side/custom function authoring, documented payments (e.g. Stripe) and email integrations, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add server-side functions and third-party integrations like payments and email from the builder

citations.quote: Describe what you want to build in the chat, and Make can create a Payload-powered backend, including a database, file storage, authentication, and an admin panel.
You can also manually connect a Supabase project from Make settings.
Figma stores it securely so your app can use it without exposing the key to visitors when you publish.
The generated Payload and Next.js code is included in your Make project.
